episode_title: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

real_qa.q: What is the mission of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory and what role does the Buildings Program play?
real_qa.r: The National Renewable Energy Laboratory is one of 17 Department of Energy national laboratories and is the only one fully committed to a mission of a clean and energy efficient and renewable energy future. Dr. Jackson manages the program that supports the Building Technologies Office at Department of Energy, ensuring resources are delivered on time and on budget while bringing science and research strategies to identify what's next in clean energy and buildings work.
real_qa.requete: National Renewable Energy Laboratory Buildings Program mission

real_qa.q: How did Dr. Roderick Jackson combine his family's construction legacy with mechanical engineering and energy research?
real_qa.r: Dr. Jackson leveraged his family's building construction legacy by integrating it with his engineering and science background. His father was a framer and all 11 of his father's brothers built houses. Rather than abandoning this legacy, Dr. Jackson brought engineering and science perspectives to take it to another level, eventually focusing his PhD research on energy in buildings—creating a marriage of family legacy with his passion for science and energy.
real_qa.requete: Roderick Jackson family construction legacy mechanical engineering

real_qa.q: What sparked Dr. Roderick Jackson's interest in energy research during his engineering education?
real_qa.r: Dr. Jackson's interest in energy was sparked in his senior design capstone course at Georgia Tech in 1996, taught by a professor who had been influential in designing the Olympic torch for the Atlanta Olympics. The professor focused heavily on energy, discussing peak oil and the importance of energy, which piqued Jackson's initial interest in pursuing a career in energy alongside his existing passion for thermodynamics.
real_qa.requete: Georgia Tech 1996 Olympic torch professor energy capstone

real_qa.q: How does Dr. Roderick Jackson integrate social justice and civil rights principles into clean energy work?
real_qa.r: Dr. Jackson was influenced by his mother's participation in the Civil Rights Movement and her emphasis on social justice. He now brings this lens to his buildings and clean energy work, ensuring that pursuing a clean energy future does not increase existing social injustices or energy inequities. He states that 'it is not enough for us to pursue a clean energy future that increases injustices that we have today,' and instead aims for an equitable and clean energy future.
real_qa.requete: clean energy social justice equity energy barriers

real_qa.q: What does clean energy mean and why is transitioning away from coal-based electricity generation important?
real_qa.r: Clean energy means generating electricity without relying on dirty fossil fuels like coal and natural gas. When coal is burned to generate electricity, it creates smoke and soot that is emitted into the atmosphere, trapping light and causing climate change. Clean energy replaces this fossil fuel-based generation with renewable sources that do not produce these harmful emissions.
real_qa.requete: clean energy coal electricity climate change emissions

real_qa.q: How did Dr. Jackson's spirituality influence his pursuit of a PhD in mechanical engineering?
real_qa.r: Dr. Jackson's spirituality served as a foundation during the difficult PhD process. He cited First Corinthians, stating 'by the grace of God, I am what I am' and noted that while he worked hard—studying in the lab while others socialized—it was still by the grace of God that he had the will to persevere. His spiritual grounding helped him during stressful moments when he questioned whether the PhD was for him, knowing he had 'something within me that is bigger than this current stressful situation.'
real_qa.requete: PhD spirituality grace God perseverance difficult

guest.bio_context: Dr. Jackson sets the strategic plan for NREL's buildings portfolio while working closely with senior laboratory management. He holds a three-year appointment to the American Council for an Energy Efficient Economy Research Advisory Board, which began in 2021. He is a 2022 Bay of STEM Conference Professional Achievement and Government Awardee and has received numerous awards including the National Gym Consortium Alumni of the Year and Greater Knoxville Business Journal's 40 Under 40. Dr. Jackson holds a PhD in mechanical engineering and earned his first engineering degree from Georgia Tech.

real_quote: It is not enough for us to pursue a clean energy future that increases injustices that we have today. We can address climate change and ensure that we are not increasing social injustices or energy inequities.
